title: Patti close
hookLine: a wedding song remembered long after a grocery list: closing the Patti, an alphabet set in a raga and signed by Nanak the poet

cards: A grocery list is gone from memory by the weekend. A song heard once at a cousin's wedding comes back years later with every word in place, because the tune held on to them.
For four days this path has read the Patti as a tablet, as letters, as a lesson. It was always a song as well, with a raga to carry it. Today we close it by listening to it that way.

teach.b: First, where it lives. The Patti doesn't sit in the Guru Granth Sahib as a school primer. It's placed in Raga Asa, among hymns that are sung, and its heading gives it a raga, which tells a musician how to sing it.
The alphabet comes with a tune attached. Second, its refrain.

teach.h: THE RAHAO PULLS THE MIND BACK.
teach.b: The Rahao, the line we spent two days with, is the center the song keeps coming back to: why do you forget, foolish mind? When you give your account, then you'll be counted educated.
Letter after letter moves forward, and the refrain pulls the mind back. That's how a song teaches. Third, how it ends.
The last stanza says, in paraphrase: the One who made everything is doing all that is done, makes it happen, and knows it all.
Thus says Nanak the poet. Saair, poet.
Guru Nanak signs his alphabet not as a schoolmaster but as a poet.

Fourth, look at what the song carried these last days: the tablet, and learning one mark at a time; sasai, the made world and one Master of all; the letters of the mind, gray hair, blame and the show we put on; and the scholar's mistake, that the real exam is a life.
Read as a list, that's a lot.
Sung, it's one thing: an alphabet turned toward God, with a tune to carry it until the heart can hold it alone.

how: Ragis sing the Patti in Raga Asa as kirtan, returning to the Rahao line between stanzas, and some sangats sing it with children learning Gurmukhi so the letters and their meanings are learned together.

games.q: you've written a poem on every letter of the alphabet. how do you sign it?
o: you don't sign it at all.
games.why: the last stanza ends: thus says Nanak the poet. saair, poet.

practice: Choose one letter's line, sasai, the One who made the world is Master of all, or dadai, I blame no one, the fault is in my deeds, and if you can, find a recording of the Patti in Raga Asa and listen for it.
If not, hum the line softly three or four times to any simple tune, even two notes going up and down, then let it go quiet and sit with whatever stays. If you pray, end with Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Patti close. Guru Nanak's alphabet, set in Raga Asa, carried by a refrain to the mind, and signed: thus says Nanak the poet. Today's word.

orig.note: saair: poet; Guru Nanak's word for himself in the Patti's closing line.

carryVoice: Your line: the alphabet sings. A tune holds what a list forgets. Rest easy.
